items.title: Bridging the gap in assist devices
items.body: COMANECI™ is the only non-occlusive and temporary device for wide-neck aneurysm treatment.
items.label: Request a demo

items.body: Minimize the risk and disruption to patients' lives with lasting results. COMANECI™ is the first active assist device – its added user control overcomes the limitations of conventional balloons and stents.
The temporary deployment of COMANECI™ provides the long-term support of a stent, achieving high packing density and 85% immediate complete occlusion compared to 79% with stent-assisted coiling.¹
items.title: require implants
items.footnote: Avoiding implants like stents is preferable to allow the brain to heal naturally and minimize long-term stroke risks and bleeding complications.

items.body: Unlike balloons, COMANECI™ provides support without blocking blood flow to the brain. Clinicians can focus on accurate placement rather than the countdown to an ischemic event. COMANECI™ demonstrates the highest complete occlusion and lowest complication rates.
items.title: blood supply

items.body: 95% successful long-term occlusion and 1% retreatment rates show the lasting durability of treatment with COMANECI in both ruptured and unruptured wide-neck aneurysms.²

link.label: Unlock SUCCESS: The prospective study data

chart.title: Successful intracranial aneurysm occlusion (Raymond Roy Classification I or II)
annotations: Raymond I+II: 86% at end of procedure → 95% at follow-up (P=0.05)

Unique braiding technology prevents flow disruption during the coiling procedure.

items.body: Operator-controlled adjustability enables adjustable vessel conformity.

items.title: A patient-centric approach to AIS
items.body: TIGERTRIEVER™ is the only active thrombectomy device – it is engineered to adapt to patient anatomy. Accelerate clot integration and reduce stress on the brain during mechanical thrombectomy procedures.
items.label: Request a demo

items.body: Unlike conventional stent retrievers, active thrombectomy can improve clot penetration¹ and facilitate smooth retrieval with adjustable radial force.
items.title: control

items.body: Two million brain cells die every minute. TIGERTRIEVER™ saves minutes when removing the clot – with reported procedure times faster than the leading competitors.
items.title: thrombectomy
items.footnote: Speed matters – TIGER Trial showed quicker time to reperfusion than using aspiration alone.

items.body: Adjustability handles patient variability in real-time. TIGERTRIEVER™ has high first-pass success (FPE) and low emboli to new territory (ENT), outperforming competitors in challenging procedures involving stenosis, hard clot, and tortuosity in patients with intracranial atherosclerosis (ICAD).

items.text: SUccess in Comaneci-assist Coils Embolization Surveillance Study
A high rate of aneurysm occlusion with Comaneci in wide-neck aneurysms, sustained at 6 months, with a favorable safety profile.
Successful occlusion (Raymond Roy I + II) rose from 86% at the end of the procedure to 95% at follow-up.
More patients with a good outcome over time
Good clinical outcome (mRS 0–2): 73% at baseline, 80% at 30 days, 82% at 6 months (P < 0.05).
No symptomatic thromboembolic events. All deaths were in ruptured cases; hemorrhages and perforations were unrelated to Comaneci.
17 US centers, from SUNY Buffalo to UCLA. Data adjudicated by an independent imaging core lab.

items.html:
Background

Comaneci™ is a novel coil embolization assist device that is retrievable, radially adjustable, and designed as an adjunct to coiling of wide-necked aneurysms without limiting blood flow. Comaneci was introduced to the US market in 2019. The objective of this FDA-regulated post-market study is to assess the safety and performance of the device in US clinical practice.

Method

SUCCESS is a multicenter, single arm, open, prospective study, enrolling 90 consecutive subjects in 17 US centers between November 2020 and October 2023. Subjects had a wide neck (4-10 mm or dome to neck ratio <2) intracranial aneurysm, ruptured or unruptured, that is suitable for coil embolization.

Results

Ninety (90) consecutive subjects were enrolled with mean age 62 (range 29-82) years. Of these, 63% were female and 36% had ruptured aneurysms. Successful Occlusion (Raymond Roy I and II) at end of procedure was 86%, and 95% at 6 month follow up (Fig. 1), good clinical outcome (mRS 0-2) was 73% at baseline, 80% at 30 days follow up and 82% at 6 months follow up (Fig. 2).

Conclusions

  • Data demonstrates a high rate of successful aneurysm occlusion when using Comaneci as an assist device in wide neck aneurysms.
  • Safety profile is favorable with low thromboembolic rates compared with other modalities, such as balloons.
